title: Indiana Dunes State Park, 1966: Three Young Women Who Never Came Home

sources.what: July 2, 1966 (a Saturday); Patricia Blough, 19, Renee Bruhl, 19, Ann Miller, 21; vanished at Indiana Dunes State Park, 'never to be seen again'; Patricia 'never came home'; last seen boarding a white boat 'occupied by one white male', about 20 to 22; clothing and personal effects found on the beach; 'the women were never found'; no suspects or persons of interest; police still 'following up on any leads'
sources.who: NBC News, Dateline Cold Case Spotlight (Feb. 2023)

sources.what: Missing since 07/02/1966 from Indiana Dunes State Park; Miller (21) of Lombard, Ill., drove her 1955 Buick, picked up Blough (19) in Westchester, Ill., and Bruhl (19) on Chicago's West Side; a spot about 100 yards from the Lake Michigan shoreline; a 14- to 16-foot white boat operated by one unidentified man; each woman's clothes, wallet or purse left on the beach; the Buick still in the lot; 'have never been seen again'; 'cases remain open but inactive and unsolved'
sources.who: The Charley Project (Ann Miller, Patricia Blough, Renee Bruhl)

sources.what: a summer Saturday, July 2, 1966, Indiana Dunes State Park; belongings left on the beach; a white boat with an unidentified young man; Miller's 1955 Buick still in the parking lot; 'no sign of the young women was ever found'; theories 'never confirmed'
sources.who: Troy Taylor, American Hauntings, 'Young Women Lost' (2014)

sources.what: 'a mystery that remains unsolved to this day' (2025); cites 1966 Chicago Tribune, AP and UPI reports
sources.who: Crime Junkie, 'Infamous: The Indiana Dunes Disappearances' (2025)

beats.text: In 1966, three young women spent a summer day at Indiana Dunes State Park. They never came home.
beats.label: INDIANA DUNES STATE PARK
beats.credit: History: NBC News Dateline; The Charley Project

beats.text: Ann Miller was 21. Patricia Blough and Renee Bruhl were 19. All three were from the Chicago area.
beats.label: SATURDAY, JULY 2, 1966
beats.credit: NBC News Dateline; The Charley Project

beats.text: On Saturday, July 2, they drove in from Illinois in Ann's car and went down to the sand by Lake Michigan.
beats.label: A SUMMER DAY

beats.text: Around noon, witnesses said, the three got into a small white boat with a young man at the wheel.
beats.label: WHAT WITNESSES SAID
beats.credit: The Charley Project; NBC News Dateline; American Hauntings

beats.text: Their clothes and belongings stayed on the beach. Ann's car stayed in the lot.
beats.label: LEFT BEHIND
beats.credit: The Charley Project; NBC News Dateline; American Hauntings

beats.text: The women were never found. Investigators chased many theories, and none was ever proven.
beats.label: NEVER FOUND
beats.credit: NBC News Dateline; The Charley Project; American Hauntings

beats.text: 60 years later, the case remains unsolved.
beats.label: A COLD CASE
beats.credit: NBC News Dateline (2023); The Charley Project

factcheck.result: Round 1: lines 1, 2, 5, 6 supported; line 4 dropped 'last saw' (a later cabin-cruiser sighting is reported) and added 'around noon'; line 3 'went down to the sand'; line 7 'remains unsolved'; map notes Porter County; fog taken out (it was a sunny day).
